authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: The Cohen Circle business combination closed and Kyivstar Group listed on Nasdaq. VEON's stake in it fell from 100% to 89.6%, and VEON booked a listing expense of US$162 million.

Management previously concluded there was substantial doubt about going concern. In the FY2025 20-F it concluded that significant doubt no longer exists, citing regained capital-markets access and new financing. This is a lifted doubt, not a new one.
The sale of the Pakistan tower business (Deodar) to Engro Corp was completed. A gain of USD 489 million is cited for it in the second quarter of 2025.
share_unit_note: filed shares 1,794,000,000 against 68,861,189 quoted (x0.0384); values are per quoted share

business_model.claim: VEON sells connectivity and digital services through local brands in five frontier markets: Bangladesh, Kazakhstan, Pakistan, Ukraine and Uzbekistan.
quotes: VEON is a leading digital operator strategically positioned across five frontier markets: Bangladesh; Kazakhstan; Pakistan; Ukraine; and Uzbekistan.

business_model.claim: Revenue comes from telecommunications and infrastructure services (voice, fixed broadband, data) and from digital services (financial services, streaming, ride-hailing, healthcare, cloud and other value-added services), sold separately or in bundles.
quotes: VEON generates revenue through the provision of comprehensive telecommunications and infrastructure services, including voice communications, fixed broadband, and data services, as well as digital services encompassing digital financial services, content streaming, ride-hailing platforms, digital healthcare solutions, cloud computing, and other value-added services.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited item for Pakistan; the price-sensitivity link is inferred from the risk-factor wording on a mass-market, price-sensitive customer base
business_model.claim: Customers are consumers and businesses. In Pakistan, the item shows 73.9 million mobile customers, of whom approximately 97.4% were on prepaid plans. Tariffs target mass-market, youth, small-office, SME and enterprise segments, and corporate customers get postpaid bundles.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, approximately 97.4% of our customers in Pakistan were on prepaid plans.

business_model.claim: The company reports five geographic segments (Pakistan, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Bangladesh), plus HQ and eliminations and Others, which are not reportable segments.
quotes: Our reportable segments currently consist of the following five geographic segments: Pakistan; Ukraine; Kazakhstan; Uzbekistan; and Bangladesh.

business_model.claim: Group revenue was 4,399 in the latest fiscal year, up from 4,004 and 3,698 in the two prior years (table in millions of US dollars). The prior-year figures were represented to conform with the current presentation.
Ukraine is a large single contributor, at approximately 26% of group revenue in the latest fiscal year, so war-related conditions there bear directly on group revenue and costs.
quotes: Our operations in Ukraine represented approximately 26% of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.

business_model.claim: Digital services are the faster-growing revenue line. In the second quarter of 2026 digital revenue was USD 342 million, up 53.6% year on year, and 26.9% of group revenue.
quotes: Digital revenue climbed 53.6% YoY to USD 342 million, with Digital EBITDA margin at 36.1%, reaching 26.9% of Group revenues.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited item; the comparison with the prior quarter is inferred from P5 and P7
business_model.claim: In the third quarter of 2026 digital revenue rose to USD 355 million, up 45.9% year on year, and was 27.2% of group revenue, up 5.4 percentage points year on year.
quotes: Digital revenue1 increased 45.9% YoY to USD 355 million, representing 27.2% of Group revenue, up 5.4 percentage points YoY.

business_model.claim: Acquisitions of digital businesses add revenue. Uklon, a ride-hailing business, improved digital revenue in the latest fiscal year, and OLX Kazakhstan was acquired for a total consideration of USD 81 million.
quotes: In March 2025, we acquired Uklon, which improved our digital revenue performance during the year ended December 31, 2025.

business_model.claim: Revenue is earned in local currencies while group-level debt and much capital spending are in US dollars. Local-currency depreciation therefore lowers reported dollar results and raises the cost of servicing dollar debt.
quotes: A significant amount of our costs, expenditures and liabilities, including capital expenditures and all group-level debt, is denominated in U.S. dollars, while our operating revenue is denominated in Ukrainian hryvnia, Pakistani rupee, Kazakhstani tenge, Bangladeshi taka and the Uzbekistani som.

business_model.basis: Stated in the income statement; the ranking is read from the printed lines
business_model.claim: The largest operating cost lines are selling, general and administrative expenses at 1,883, depreciation at 578, cost of services, equipment and accessories at 526, and amortization at 224, against revenue of 4,399 (table in millions).

Inflation and energy prices drive costs. The blended electricity tariff paid by the Ukrainian operations rose 19.5% in the latest year after 27.3% the year before, and war-related security, fuel and mitigation costs were US$34 million.
quotes: For example, the blended electricity tariff (the average price we pay for electricity) for our Ukrainian operations increased by 19.5% in 2025 and 27.3% in 2024.

business_model.basis: The model and lease payments are stated; the link between the two is inferred
business_model.claim: The company follows an asset-light model: it sold tower and other infrastructure assets and leases them back under long-term arrangements. Lease payments were 250 against 150 a year earlier (table in millions), and sales of subsidiaries produced a gain of 400.
quotes: In several markets, we have completed transactions for the sale of tower and other infrastructure assets in favor of long-term lease, right-of-use, and service arrangements.

business_model.claim: Capital spending is largely maintenance of existing networks. Purchases of property and equipment were 733 and of intangible assets 216 (table in millions), and the 2026 capex intensity outlook excluding Ukraine is 15% to 17% of revenues.
quotes: We believe each of our connectivity businesses are well-invested, so our group capital expenditures are primarily focused on maintaining current business operations rather than updating assets to grow our business or increase efficiency.

business_model.basis: Figures stated in the statements; the cost-driver reading is inferred
business_model.claim: Financing costs are a large cost. Finance costs were 535 against finance income of 52, with debt and derivatives of 4,043 non-current and 1,102 current at year-end (table in millions).

business_model.basis: Ownership and proceeds are stated; the effect on attributable earnings is inferred
business_model.claim: Kyivstar is held through a listed subsidiary. VEON's ownership fell from 89.6% to 83.6% after a secondary offering that gave net proceeds of approximately US$140 million, so a smaller share of Ukrainian earnings accrues to VEON owners.
quotes: Following completion of the offering, VEON's ownership in KGL decreased from 89.6% to 83.6% and VEON received net proceeds of approximately US$140 million for general corporate purposes.

business_model.claim: Pakistan includes a banking operation. The group's cash includes USD 510 million related to banking operations in Pakistan, which is excluded from net debt, so part of reported cash backs customer deposits.
quotes: Cash and cash equivalents include USD 510 million relating to banking operations in Pakistan which is excluded for calculation of net debt.

business_model.claim: Management expects growth to continue: the 2026 outlook was raised to 16%-18% for revenue growth and 10%-12% for EBITDA growth, in US dollar terms.
quotes: Revenue growth outlook now 16%-18% YoY (previously 15%-18%), EBITDA growth outlook now 10%-12% YoY (previously 9% to 12%).

quotes: VEON is a leading digital operator strategically positioned across five frontier markets: Bangladesh; Kazakhstan; Pakistan; Ukraine; and Uzbekistan.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (company's own assertion)
competitive_position.claim: In Pakistan, the company says its operating company is the market leader, with 73.9 million mobile customers at year-end. This is the only market-position statement in the evidence.
quotes: PMCL remains the market leader in Pakistan’s telecommunications industry.

competitive_position.basis: inferred from the income statement figures
competitive_position.claim: Scale and profitability grew over the three years shown. Revenue was 4,399 (table in millions) against 4,004 a year earlier, and operating profit was 1,439 (table in millions).

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (company releases)
competitive_position.claim: The digital business is the stated growth driver. In 2Q26 digital revenue rose 53.6% to USD 342 million, or 26.9% of Group revenues. In 3Q26 it reached 27.2% of revenue, up 45.9%.
quotes: Digital revenue climbed 53.6% YoY to USD 342 million, with Digital EBITDA margin at 36.1%, reaching 26.9% of Group revenues.

competitive_position.claim: Group revenue growth is double-digit. 3Q26 revenue rose 17.2% to USD 1,307 million, and management has raised the mid-point of its full-year outlook.
quotes: Total revenue increased 17.2% YoY to USD 1,307 million.

competitive_position.claim: The company follows an asset-light model. It sold its Pakistan tower business to Engro Corp and leases the infrastructure back under a long-term agreement. This frees resources for customer-facing and digital initiatives but makes it a tenant of its own network sites.
quotes: VEON will continue to lease Deodar’s extensive infrastructure for the provision of nationwide mobile voice and data services under a long-term partnership agreement.

competitive_position.claim: The company is investing to defend its Pakistan position. Jazz secured 190 MHz in a spectrum auction, to be paid in rupees from the following year, and management ties higher capex intensity to this.
quotes: Jazz secured the allocation of 190 MHz after a successful mobile spectrum auction held in Pakistan

competitive_position.claim: The company is widening its digital ecosystem through acquisitions. Beeline Kazakhstan completed the purchase of OLX KZ for USD 81 million.
quotes: OLX KZ is a scaled platform for goods, services, real estate and automotive listings, reaching more than 52% of Kazakhstan’s active internet population with approximately 9 million monthly active users.

competitive_position.claim: Management has set out a 2030 framework that targets organic annual growth in USD revenue and EBITDA of 12–15% and aspires to a 50% digital revenue mix. This is a company target, not an outcome.
quotes: Aspires to reach 50% digital revenue mix

competitive_position.claim: The largest named threat is the war in Ukraine. Ukraine was about 26% of revenue, and the filing cites network damage, sanctions and the risk of nationalization of Kyivstar.
quotes: Our operations in Ukraine represented approximately 26% of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.

competitive_position.claim: The company is exposed to currency mismatch. Group-level debt and many costs are in US dollars while revenue is earned in five local currencies, so local-currency depreciation hurts reported results and debt servicing.
quotes: A significant amount of our costs, expenditures and liabilities, including capital expenditures and all group-level debt, is denominated in U.S. dollars, while our operating revenue is denominated in Ukrainian hryvnia, Pakistani rupee, Kazakhstani tenge, Bangladeshi taka and the Uzbekistani som.

competitive_position.claim: Bangladesh faces political and inflationary pressure. Inflation peaked at 9.94% in the year and cut consumer spending on telecoms, and the filing flags a possible impairment of the Bangladesh unit.
quotes: Elevated inflation has negatively affected consumer spending appetite and altered telecommunications spending patterns, which in turn has had a corresponding adverse impact on our results of operations during the relevant period.

competitive_position.claim: Regulatory and tax disputes in Pakistan are a named threat. After an adverse court ruling, the Deodar tax risk was moved from remote to probable, and the company recognized an additional tax expense of US$122 million as part of a composite settlement framework.
quotes: management updated its judgment regarding the Deodar tax case, reclassifying the risk from remote to probable, and recognized the related tax exposure as a provision.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (risk factor summary)

quotes: risks relating to developments from competition, unforeseen or otherwise, in each of the countries in which we operate, including our ability to keep pace with technological changes and evolving industry standards;
